walkthroughs.body_html:
The world acts together through treaties.

The Kyoto Protocol (1997) set early targets.

The Paris Agreement (2015) targets well below 2 degrees C.

CITES protects wildlife.

It restricts trade in around 38,000 species, including elephants and rhinos.

The treaty entered into force in 1975.

Action also happens locally.

Cities promote cycling, recycling and renewables.

Individuals can cut emissions through diet and travel choices.

mcqs.q: Why can a cold winter NOT disprove climate change?
options: A really cold winter proves global warming is not happening.
It is the hole in the ozone layer letting in more sun.
Climate is the long-term statistical average; a single cold winter is a weather event. Climate change is the trend in averages and extremes over decades, not the absence of cold days.
Climate change only happens in summer.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between mitigation and adaptation to climate change?
options: Mitigation reduces the causes (cutting greenhouse gas emissions); adaptation reduces the impacts (e.g. building sea walls, drought-resistant crops, early warning systems).
Mitigation is done by HICs and adaptation is done by LICs.
Mitigation and adaptation mean the same thing — both are about stopping climate change.
It is the hole in the ozone layer letting in more sun.

mcqs.q: What is the enhanced greenhouse effect?
options: Mitigation is done by HICs and adaptation is done by LICs.
It is the hole in the ozone layer letting in more sun.
The greenhouse effect is entirely man-made and harmful.
The strengthening of the natural greenhouse effect by human activities (mainly burning fossil fuels) which add CO2 and other gases to the atmosphere.
